pages.title: Learning and Understanding Rouh
pages.intro: Rouh is currently the most powerful assistant, beyond Claude, Muse, OpenClaw, Hermes and others. To wield that power, you need to understand what Rouh is, how it operates and why it is different than anything else. So it made that guide to itself.

hero.title: Your path to everything Rouh can do
hero.fresh: Start with the first tip. Each takes a minute or two, and Rouh ticks most of them by itself when it sees you do them.
hero.done: You have done every tip on the path.

talk_note.text: Say it in the message box at the bottom of the chat, typed or with the microphone. The answer appears in the chat; pages and tables appear on the canvas.

terms_note: Words of Rouh's own, explained where they stand (review 49, problem 433). Petar, 22 November 2026: as a rule, a card's title and outcome never use a word a later tip teaches; say it in plain words. On a tip's page, the first time one of these words stands in a tip other than the one that teaches it, it can be pressed for what it means, and for the tip that teaches it.

silo.means: A silo is one part of your life, such as Work or Personal, kept apart from the others.

orb.means: The orb is the round button in the bottom-left corner: the live picture of what Rouh is doing, and the button that opens the menu.

canvas.means: The canvas is the space beside the chat where pages, tables and pictures appear.

Clockwork.means: Clockwork is where Rouh keeps your reminders and the work it does on repeat.

heartbeat.means: The heartbeat is the work Rouh does by itself, on a schedule, without being asked.

Synapse.means: Synapse is Rouh's memory: what it knows about people, places and your work, and where it learned it.

Anatomy.means: Anatomy is the group of the menu with Rouh's own settings: what it is made of and how it behaves.

Evolution.means: Evolution is where Rouh tries out new abilities, and you keep or reject them.

Vocabulary.means: Vocabulary is where Rouh keeps your own words and nicknames, and what you mean by them.

Metabolism.means: Metabolism is the page that lists every piece of work Rouh is doing in the background, and what each one is doing now.

Boxes.means: A box is a safe for a secret, such as a password: what you put in it is sealed, and the AI never sees it.

stages.title: Meet Rouh

lessons.title: What Rouh is
lessons.outcome: After this you know what Rouh is and why it is different from every other assistant.

cover.alt: Rouh's orb: a glowing white core, which is this machine, with turquoise tentacles, branches and coloured twigs, each one work running right now.

summary: Rouh is a cutting edge experimental AI that has all the standard capabilities of AI assistants, but is much more than that - it feels and behaves like a living thing and acts like your avatar to augment your capabilities and reach.

The major difference between Rouh and everything else is that rouh's code is not fixed. You can ask it to change in any way and acquire any capability and it will. By observing your actions and data, Rouh also self-evolves on its own with new features and modifications to support you in your goals.

So Rouh evolves constantly, you evolve because you become more capable thanks to its help and therefore you are in a continuous co-evolution setup together. This setup where the software you use is not fixed but continuously evolves may be a bit awkward at first but once you use it, you will find there is no other way forwards - both personally and in an organization.
A couple more things are worth mentioning now, and will be explained in detail in other tips:

points.text: Rouh has a very special memory setup (The Synapse), where it remembers everything and everything is connected. As a result, after a while it feels like a person and the answers are astonishingly relevant. To make this work, you need a special service that costs you about $1-5/mo depending on the usage.

Rouh.land is the motherland. While your Rouh can be fully independent and disconnected, it is much better if it connects with the rouh.land service. It is free and has a number of benefits such as extra security, updates, sharing securely your collaborative work, shared pool of features to steal functionalities (known as Gene Pool), cost optimization updates. A connected rouh is a much more powerful and capable rouh.
Rouhs can collaborate on tasks live. And you can be part of that or watch them.
Rouh has a special Task system where your work is organized. You will see how this is much more useful than scattered documents and chats to which you are used.

closing: There are plenty of innovations and things you haven't seen, each making you more powerful and more capable in completing whatever tasks you decide.
Remember - the current Rouh is just your starting blank canvas. Everybody's Rouh is different and it starts evolving the moment it is born. There is no limit.

lessons.title: Rouh lives on its own machine
lessons.outcome: After this you know why Rouh runs on a computer of its own, and what that computer needs.
summary: Rouh runs on one computer of its own, not inside your browser. The browser, on a desk or a phone, is a window onto it.
how: It stays on. The heartbeat, Clockwork and the night jobs run on that machine while you are away. Work that falls due while it is off or asleep waits until it is back.
It keeps its own data there: the database, your workspace (a private git repository of its own), its own code, and nightly copies of the database.
It changes its own code there. Every change goes through its protected core, which Rouh itself cannot change, and can be undone.
It is not an administrator of that machine. Its parts run in locked-down containers, and its work reaches the rest of the machine only when you allow it on Permissions.
It installs on Linux (Ubuntu and Debian are tested): a server you reach over SSH, a desktop, or a virtual machine, on Intel or Arm. Rouh for Mac runs it on a Mac.
The installer asks for at least 2 cores, 4 GB of memory and 15 GB of free disk, and 4 cores, 8 GB and 64 GB to run well.
The rings round the orb show that machine: its storage, its CPU and its memory.

lessons.title: Reach your Rouh from anywhere
lessons.outcome: After this you can open your Rouh on any computer or phone, and know what is open to the internet.
summary: Your Rouh's machine can sit behind a home router with nothing opened to the internet. A Rouh connected to rouh.land gets its own address, https://its-name.rouh.page, through rouh.land's relay, from the moment it is born.
how: The machine dials out to the relay and keeps that line open, so no port, domain or router setting is needed.
Find the address in the menu: Anatomy, Your Rouh, under Your Rouh's URL. The first start shows it too.
Open it on any computer or phone and sign in: type your email and press Continue with email. Rouh then offers your passkey, or emails you a link and a six-digit code, or asks for your password.
On a phone the quickest way is the code: on your computer press Show sign-in code under Your Rouh's URL, and scan it with the phone's camera. It works once, for ten minutes.
The connection stays locked from your browser to your machine: the relay passes it on by its name and cannot read it. Only the web app is reachable that way, and every page needs a sign-in.
To take access away: Turn off, under Your Rouh's URL, stops phones reaching it. Sign out, under Anatomy, You, Your account, ends this browser, and changing your password signs out every browser.
Nobody else has an account on your Rouh: you share single tasks instead. A Rouh not connected to rouh.land has no address and opens nothing to the internet.

lessons.title: The Orb: The most important button
lessons.outcome: After this you can open the menu with the orb, read how busy this machine is, and see every piece of work Rouh is doing.
summary: The orb is the round button in the bottom-left corner. It is the menu button, a gauge of the machine Rouh runs on, and a live picture of everything Rouh is doing.

sections.title: The orb as a button
text: Press it once: the menu opens from the left, with every part of Rouh. The orb becomes a row at the foot of the menu: a cross, Close menu, and beside it a slim view of the orb, Open the orb.
Press and hold it for half a second to open the orb over the whole screen straight away.
While Rouh is at rest, with nothing running, it shows three lines, the sign of a menu, with its rings still round it. The moment Rouh answers or starts work, the live picture comes back.

Drag it, or flick it. While you hold it, it follows your finger or mouse anywhere; let go and it settles at the bottom left or the bottom right. It stays on that side in this browser until you drag it back. With the orb in focus, the left and right arrow keys move it too.
It works the same at every width. On a phone it sits a little higher, above the message box. The menu always opens from the left, whichever side the orb is on.

image.alt: The foot of the open menu: the orb has become a row, with the cross that closes the menu and a slim view of the orb beside it.

marks.label: Open the orb over the whole screen

sections.title: The rings: this machine
text: The coloured rings round the small orb show the machine Rouh runs on, read every three seconds. Each is an arc from twelve o'clock, as long as its share. From the outside in:
Storage: light grey, amber from 65% used, red above 80%.
CPU: green, amber from 50% busy, red above 70%.
Memory: baby blue, purple from half used, red from three quarters.

When something is waiting on you, the faint edge round them turns red. Point at a ring with the mouse to read it, such as CPU of this machine: 12% busy. Over the whole screen the same numbers sit in the bottom-right corner: cpu, proc, ram and disk.

image.alt: The small orb with work running: the storage, CPU and memory rings on its right, and its edge red because something waits on you.

marks.label: The edge: red while something waits on you

after: The core in the middle is this machine too. Drawn in 3D it is a white light with a halo: turquoise-white while work runs, red while something waits on you. Where a browser cannot draw in 3D, a flat orb is drawn instead; its three thin crossing rings and the slow breathing ring round the core say only whether Rouh is idle, working or waiting on you, not the machine's numbers.

sections.title: The tentacles: work running now
text: Every piece of work Rouh is doing grows out of the core. Here is the orb over the whole screen while work runs.

image.alt: The orb over the whole screen while work runs: turquoise branches out of the core with coloured twigs, Rouh's own pale branch, a red dashed branch marked NEEDS YOU, and a finished branch fading.

marks.label: A background job: a turquoise branch out of the core
A helper inside the job: a thinner turquoise branch off it
A tool call: a short coloured twig, longer the longer it ran
Rouh's own answer: a branch in the core's pale colour
Waiting on you: red and dashed, with a square and NEEDS YOU
Finished work: fades, holds at half, turns to a grey trace, then goes

swatches.words: A connector or service, such as mail or the calendar

after: In 3D the marks show in the tip that appears when you point at a twig, and on its card; the flat orb draws them at the twig's tip.
No lines means nothing is running: only the core is there.

sections.title: Opening the orb over the whole screen
text: Open it three ways: press and hold the small orb; press the orb and then Open the orb in the menu; or ask Rouh, Show me the orb.

Over the whole screen, point at any part, the core included, to see what it is, and press it to open its card: This machine, A background job, A helper inside a job, A tool call, or Rouh itself. Drag to turn it; R brings it back to the whole view.

At the top right are What the models cost, Sound, Orb settings and the cross, which puts the orb back in its corner. Escape does the same, one step at a time, and so does any new card arriving on the canvas. Or ask Rouh, Put the orb away.

lessons.title: Find your way round the screen
lessons.outcome: After this you know the four parts of Rouh's screen, and what each word for them means.

cover.alt: Rouh's screen at a desk: the conversation on the left and the content space, the canvas, on the right.

summary: Rouh's screen has four parts, and every tip after this one names them. Here is what each is called and what it is for.

parts.name: The conversation
parts.text: Where you and Rouh talk, with the message box at the bottom. Type or speak there; Rouh answers there.

parts.name: The canvas, Rouh's content space
parts.text: The wide space beside the conversation, where Rouh shows what is easier to see than to read: a page, a table, a plan, a picture. When a tip says the canvas, it means this space.

parts.name: The orb, which is also the menu button
parts.text: The round button in the bottom-left corner: press it for the menu with every part of Rouh. When a tip says open the menu, press the orb.

parts.name: The buttons at the top
parts.text: Small round buttons at the top of each page, such as a plus to add something, a magnifying glass to search, and a speech bubble that brings the conversation back. Point at one, or hold it, to see its name.

says: What is on my screen right now?
Open the menu for me.

lessons.title: Who you pay, and for what
lessons.outcome: After this you know the two ways Rouh is paid for: your API keys, and your plans.
summary: Rouh never sends you a bill. You pay the AI companies directly, in two ways.

Your chats, and almost everything else Rouh asks a model, are paid per use through your own API keys: the company counts the words, as tokens, and bills your account. Long background work, done by Claude Code or Codex, runs on your Claude or ChatGPT plan instead.
how: Chats always need an API key, from Anthropic or OpenAI. A Claude plan cannot answer the chats.
Claude Code runs, which are Rouh's background jobs and runs, use your Claude plan once it is signed in. Without a plan they fall back to your Anthropic key, paid per use.
Codex runs use your ChatGPT plan, unless you choose to bill them to your OpenAI key.

Your keys are on the Models page under Providers (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour, Models). Other services, such as voice and search by meaning, have keys of their own under Anatomy, Connections, Keys, and bill you on their own accounts.
says: Which of my keys are set up?

lessons.title: See what one answer cost
lessons.outcome: After this you can read the cost of every answer in the chat.
summary: Every answer says what it cost, at its top and under it.

how.text: At the top of an answer, a small grey line ends with the time it took and its cost. The tip Read the line above an answer says what opening it shows.

image.alt: One answer in the chat, numbered: its time and cost at the top, the Cheaper and Smart buttons, and the tokens and cost under it.

marks.label: Time and cost of this answer
Cheaper or Smart: answer again on the other
Tokens in and out, how much came from the cache, and the cost

how: Under the answer, a small grey line counts the tokens in and out, how many requests it took, how much came from the cache, and the cost. Under a cent it shows cents, such as 0.42c.
In Chat Options, Last message says how many tokens the last turn sent, and how many came from the cache.

lessons.title: Open What the models cost
lessons.outcome: After this you can see what Rouh spent, on what, day by day.

cover.alt: What the models cost, opened from the orb: the period chips, an example total paid per use, calls, the average a message and the bars day by day, coloured by use.

summary: One screen adds up everything paid per use: What the models cost. It lives in the orb. An administrator sees the whole organisation; everyone else sees their own calls. The amounts in the picture are only an example.
how: Open the orb over the whole screen: press the orb, then the row Open the orb in the menu. Or press and hold the orb.
At the top right, beside the sound button, press the bars: What the models cost.
Pick a period: Day, Week, Month, 30 days or Range. The big number is what was paid per use, with the number of calls and the average for a message.
Split by Use, Company, Model, Day, or Chat, job or page. Press any bar or row to go one level down; Up one level, or Escape, comes back.
See the calls lists each call with its tokens and cost. Press one to see what the cost is made of, with the price a million tokens.
The box at the right says what the numbers leave out, such as runs paid by your plans.

lessons.title: Choose which AI answers
lessons.outcome: After this you know which model answers, and how to trade quality for cost.

cover.alt: Models: the mode, Best, Balanced or Saver, and the providers.

summary: Trade quality for cost with one setting or one sentence.
how: Open Models (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour). Only an administrator can change it.
Pick a mode: Best answers every chat on Smart, Saver every chat on Cheaper, and Balanced lets Rouh pick Cheaper when a message is easy.
Saver puts every use paid per use on Cheaper too, and warns that unattended work on the cheap model can make mistakes.
Each tier, Cheaper and Smart, has a model; every use of an AI in Rouh is on one of them.
Or say what you want, and Rouh changes the setting for you.
says: Which model answers my chats, and which mode are you in?
Switch to Saver.

lessons.title: Trade quality for cost in a sentence
lessons.outcome: After this you trade quality for cost with one sentence.

cover.alt: Models: the mode, Best, Balanced or Saver, and the providers.

summary: Pick Best, Balanced or Saver by asking, without opening Settings.
how: Say which mode you want: Best, Balanced or Saver.
Rouh switches without you opening Settings.
says: Switch to Saver.

lessons.title: Why models cost different amounts
lessons.outcome: After this you know what makes one model dearer than another, and where to see it.
summary: A model is priced per million tokens, words in and words out. A smarter model costs many times more for the same words. Rouh keeps two tiers: Cheaper, for easy work, and Smart, for the rest.
how: Rouh fetches the current prices once a day, with the model standard from rouh.land, so they are never written into a tip.
To see a price, open What the models cost, press See the calls and pick one call: What the cost is made of shows the price a million for each part.
Words Rouh has read recently come from the cache, far cheaper than fresh ones. Rouh caches by itself; nothing to switch.
Each use of a model in Rouh is on one of the tiers. They are listed on the Models page under Customise, Each use, each with why it starts where it does.

lessons.title: Run long work on your plans
lessons.outcome: After this background work runs on your Claude or ChatGPT plan, not per use.
summary: Claude Code and Codex runs can use the monthly plan you already pay for. On a plan a run costs nothing per use; it uses up the plan's allowance instead.
how: Sign in Claude Code: the Claude plan on the Models page under Agents' sign-ins, or the Subscriptions card under Anatomy, Connections. Press Sign in with Claude and follow its steps.
Sign in Codex the same way: Sign in Codex with ChatGPT.
The Subscriptions card shows each plan's 5-hour window and Weekly window, how much is used and when it resets.
A Codex run on a plan that runs out pauses and asks before anything goes to your OpenAI key. In Start a run, Billed to chooses the plan or the key for one run.
What the models cost counts runs on plans, but gives them no dollars. A Claude Code run that fell back to your Anthropic key is not priced in Rouh at all: only Anthropic's own console shows it.

lessons.title: What background work costs
lessons.outcome: After this you know what drives the cost of jobs, the heartbeat, quests and night work.
summary: Work Rouh does while you are away uses model time too. What it costs depends on how often it runs, and whether it runs on a plan or a key.
how: Jobs and runs are Claude Code or Codex: on a plan they use its windows, on a key they cost per use. Metabolism (menu, Evolution) lists them; Stop ends one.
The heartbeat is off on a new Rouh. When on, each beat with something to do starts a job. Its Settings tab sets a daily cap on what beats may cost per use, and Today shows what was spent against it.
Each quest can have a budget. Quests shows what it spent against it, and a quest whose budget is spent waits.
Clockwork runs what is due, and a repeat that does something is a turn of Rouh each time. Pause one from its row's menu.
Anatomy, Meta, What Rouh keeps and runs lists every night job, each with a Money line saying what it may cost, and an On or Off switch.
says: What is running right now?
What did the heartbeat spend today?

lessons.title: What memory and long chats cost
lessons.outcome: After this you know what remembering, searching and long chats cost.
summary: Memory makes every answer a little dearer, because Rouh looks things up and sends what it found with your message. Long chats cost more for the same reason: the model reads them again each time.
how: Before an answer, two small models read your message and Synapse searches your memory. Simple chat and incognito skip this.
Searching by meaning uses a separate service, with its own key and bill (Search by meaning, under Anatomy, Connections, Keys).
At night, dreaming tidies memory with model calls, up to a spend cap. Synapse, Dreams shows each night's cost; Tune sets the cap.
General sends only its newest messages and a short summary of the rest. Every other chat is sent whole each time, so a long chat costs more for every message. A new chat starts cheap again.

lessons.title: Spend less
lessons.outcome: After this you know the ways Rouh offers to spend less.
summary: Every saving here is a setting Rouh really has. Pick the ones that fit how you work.
how: Choose Saver, or Balanced with Cheaper used more often (Models, Customise, When Balanced uses Cheaper). Or pick Cheap for one chat.
Put single uses on Cheaper, or Off where that is offered, on the Models page under Customise, Each use.
Sign in your Claude and ChatGPT plans, so long work runs on them instead of per use.
Use Simple chat for plain questions, and start a new chat instead of carrying on a very long one.
Keep the heartbeat off or paused, give quests a budget, and turn off night jobs you do not need under What Rouh keeps and runs.
Turn off Compare answers blind on the Models page: each comparison asks a second model too.
Tidying away finished runs saves nothing: a finished run spends nothing.
says: Switch to Saver.
Pause the heartbeat.

lessons.title: Set a spending limit
lessons.outcome: After this a runaway month cannot cost more than you set.
summary: Rouh has caps for its own background work, but no cap on everything at once. The limit that holds for everything is the one you set with the AI company.
how: In each company's own console, set a monthly spending limit on your key. The key steps on Rouh's first start show where.
When a company refuses because its limit is reached, Rouh says once that its spending limit is reached, and where to raise it. Until then, chats and anything else on that company's models fail.
Inside Rouh: the heartbeat's daily cap, each quest's budget, and dreaming's cap a night.
A card's caps on Anatomy, Money, Payments are for real purchases, which always wait for your yes. They are not model costs.

lessons.title: Bills Rouh does not show
lessons.outcome: After this you know which costs you will only see on another company's bill.
summary: Some services Rouh uses bill you on their own accounts, and Rouh does not count them.
how: Voice, hearing and speaking, is ElevenLabs, on its own key. Voice replies off means nothing is spoken.
Search by meaning, LinkedIn look-ups, YouTube and others each use their own key under Anatomy, Connections, Keys, with their own bills.
Runs on your Claude or ChatGPT plan are paid by the plan, and a Claude Code run that fell back to your Anthropic key shows only on Anthropic's console.
Pictures are counted: they show under their own use on What the models cost.

lessons.title: Set up the chat
lessons.outcome: After this the chat can answer you.
summary: Rouh needs an AI service to answer in the chat. Until one is connected, the chat says Chat is not set up yet. Everything else in Rouh still works.
how: Press Set up chat in that message. It opens the Models page.
Follow what the Models page says for the AI company you choose. Each answer costs a little, usually a few cents.
If someone else set up Rouh for you, ask them to do this.

lessons.title: Talk to Rouh
lessons.outcome: After this you know where to type to Rouh, and where its answers appear.
summary: Everything starts with a sentence. You type it in the message box at the bottom of the chat, or say it out loud. This is the one place you talk to Rouh: every tip after this one says what to say, and you say it here.

how.text: Open the chat: press the round button at the bottom left to open the menu, then press Rouh, circled in red below. The chat opens, with the message box at the bottom.

Rouh: press it to open the chat

how.text: Tap the message box, the wide box at the bottom that says Type to Rouh, and type what you want, in plain words.

Rouh's answer appears in the chat, under your words.
The chat and the page you were on take turns on a phone: the button at the top right switches between them, so this tip is one tap away.

Rouh: press it to open the chat

how.text: Find the message box: the wide box at the bottom of the chat that says Type to Rouh. Press it and type what you want, in plain words.

image.alt: A cut-out of the chat on a phone, numbered: your question, Rouh's answer listing what it can do, the message box and the blue Send arrow.

how: Press Enter to send, or press the blue arrow at the right end of the box. Shift with Enter starts a new line.
Rouh's answer appears in the chat, under your words. Pages, tables and pictures appear on the canvas, the space beside the chat where pages open (the next tips show it).

how.text: If you cannot see the chat, it has been put away to a narrow bar at the left of the screen. Press that bar, Show the chat, and it comes back.

Call this chat Holiday plans.
What did I ask you yesterday?
Explain that more simply.
lessons.without_chat: Without the chat there is nobody to answer yet. Set it up first, then come back to this lesson.

lessons.title: Ask for several things in one breath
lessons.outcome: After this you can ask for several things in one message.
summary: You do not have to wait between requests. Say them together and Rouh does each one.
how: Say or type everything you want in one message, joined with and.
Rouh does each one and says what it did for each.
says: Remind me on Friday at nine to call Sam, and put lunch with Lena on Thursday at one.

lessons.title: Talk by voice
lessons.outcome: After this you can talk to Rouh with your hands free, and hear it answer.

cover.alt: The Voice panel open above the message box, with Turn on the microphone, Voice replies and Dictate.

summary: You can speak to Rouh instead of typing. The voice controls are under one button at the left end of the message box. Nothing listens until you turn the microphone on.

how.text: Press the Voice button: the small person with sound waves, first on the left under the message box. A panel opens above it. On a narrow phone it is inside the paperclip's menu, under Voice.

image.alt: The Voice button and its panel, numbered: the button, the microphone, voice replies and dictate.

how: Press Turn on the microphone. Allow the microphone if the browser asks. Speak, and Rouh answers when you pause.
Voice replies decides whether Rouh reads its answers out loud. Leave it on to listen, or turn it off to read.
For a long message, press Dictate, say all of it, then press Dictate again. A pause never ends your turn. At a computer, Ctrl, Shift and Space does the same as pressing Dictate.
Press the microphone again to turn it off. Off means off: nothing is heard until you turn it on again.
says: Hi Rouh, can you hear me?
Read me my next three calendar events.
Stop talking.
Talk more slowly.

lessons.title: Stop a turn
lessons.outcome: After this you can stop Rouh in the middle of an answer, and you know what keeps going.

cover.alt: The chat, with the message box at the bottom and its blue Send button at the right end.

summary: Sometimes you have heard enough. Stop, or Escape, ends Rouh's answer where it is: its words, its thinking and its voice. Background jobs, tasks and runs it already started carry on.

how.text: While Rouh is answering and the message box is empty, the blue Send button at the right end of the box turns into Stop.

image.alt: The right end of the message box, numbered: Send, which becomes Stop while Rouh answers.

marks.label: Send, and Stop while Rouh answers

how: Press Stop, or press Escape. The answer ends where it was, and a line under it says that background work carries on.
To see what is still going, ask what is running. To stop a run too, say so, or press Stop on the run's own view on the canvas.
says: Tell me a long story about the sea.
What is running right now?
Stop that run.

lessons.title: Add to your message while Rouh answers
lessons.outcome: After this you can correct or add to a request without stopping Rouh.
summary: You do not have to wait for an answer to finish. A message you send while Rouh is answering does not stop it: Rouh reads it at its next step and takes it into account.
how: While Rouh is answering, type in the message box. Send comes back in place of Stop.
Press Send. Your message shows as waiting until Rouh has read it.
To end the answer instead, empty the box and press Stop, or press Escape.
says: Actually, make it for four people.
And add the train times.

lessons.title: Use the canvas, the space where pages appear
lessons.outcome: After this you know where pages, tables and pictures appear, and how to change them.

cover.alt: The screen at a desk: the chat on the left and the canvas on the right, holding a page.

summary: The canvas is Rouh's content space: the wide panel beside the conversation, where Rouh puts what is easier to see than to read, such as a page, a table, a plan or a picture. Every card on it has its own address, so you can open it again later or send it to someone.

how.text: Ask for something to look at, such as a page or a table. It opens on the canvas, to the right of the chat.

image.alt: The chat and the canvas side by side, numbered, with the button that puts the canvas away.

how: Ask for changes in plain words, such as Make it shorter. Rouh redraws the card, and keeps every version.
The panel button in the canvas's top right corner, Hide the canvas, puts it away to a narrow bar on the right; press that bar to bring it back. The cross beside it closes the page that is open.
On a phone the canvas is behind the chat: press the button at the top right to switch to it and back.
To keep a card with your work, ask Rouh to file it into a task.
says: Make a page with a three-day plan for Lisbon.
Show that as a table.
Make it shorter.
File that card as a step of the Lisbon task.

lessons.title: Change a card, do not ask for a new one
lessons.outcome: After this you change a card in place instead of starting again.

cover.alt: The screen at a desk: the chat on the left and the canvas on the right, holding a page.

summary: Ask for a change to the card on the screen and Rouh revises it in place. Every version is kept, so you can go back.
how: With a card on the canvas, say what to change in it.
Rouh revises that card in place and keeps every version.
Ask what it said before to go back to an earlier version.
says: What did that table say before you changed it?

lessons.title: Bring back an earlier card
lessons.outcome: After this you can find any card Rouh showed you and put it on the canvas again.
summary: Every card Rouh shows is kept and numbered: its head shows #4, for example. Where the card was in the conversation, a line stays behind with its number and title.
how: Scroll up the conversation to the card's line, such as #4 and its title.
While the card is out on the canvas, the line says On the canvas, with Bring it back here. Once the canvas has moved on, it says Open on the canvas.
Press it, or just ask for the card by its number.
To keep a card with your work for good, ask Rouh to file it into a task.
says: Show card 4 again.
File card 4 in the Lisbon task.

lessons.title: Use the chat on a phone
lessons.outcome: After this you can move between the chat and the canvas on a phone.

cover.alt: A phone showing the chat: a question, Rouh's answer, the small buttons under each, a fork's mark, and the message box.

summary: On a phone the chat and the canvas take turns on the screen. One button, at the top right, switches between them.

how.text: In the chat, the button at the top right is a square: Open the canvas. When the canvas has something new, its lines turn orange.

image.alt: A phone showing the chat: a question, Rouh's answer, the small buttons under each, a fork's mark, and the message box.

how: On the canvas the same button is a speech bubble, Show the conversation. Press it to go back.

On a phone, cards stay in the conversation and open full screen when pressed. Cards open in Chat or Canvas, over the canvas, changes that: Canvas sends every new card out to the canvas as it is drawn.
The return key starts a new line; send with the blue arrow. When the line is too narrow, Voice and Make a picture are inside the paperclip.

lessons.title: Copy, ask again or change a message
lessons.outcome: After this you know the small buttons under every message.
summary: Under every message there is a row of small buttons. Point at one, or hold it, to see its name.

how.text: Under your own message: Ask this again, Copy this message, Edit this message and ask again, and When this was sent.

image.alt: A phone showing the chat: a question, Rouh's answer, the small buttons under each, a fork's mark, and the message box.

how: Under an answer: Answer this again, Copy this answer, Read this aloud, Say it more simply, and When this was written.
Edit opens your words in place with Cancel, Fork and Send. Send asks again with the new words.
Once an answer has been asked again, arrows and a count such as 2 of 3 move between its versions.
says: Answer that again, more briefly.

lessons.title: Attach a file or a screenshot
lessons.outcome: After this you can give Rouh a picture, a PDF or a document to read.
summary: Rouh reads what you give it: pictures, PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, slides, text and code.
how: Press the paperclip, Attach files, under the message box, and pick one file or several.
Or drop files anywhere on the conversation, or paste a screenshot straight into the message box.
Each file shows as a chip above the box and uploads at once. Type your question, or send the file alone.
Almost any file up to 512 MB works; programs cannot be attached. A zip or a video reaches Rouh by name, for background work to open.
says: What does this error mean?
Sum up this PDF in five lines.

lessons.title: Make or change a picture
lessons.outcome: After this you can have Rouh draw a picture, and change part of one.
summary: Rouh can draw a picture from a description, and change part of a picture you already have.
how: Press Make a picture under the message box. The box now asks for a picture, and a Picture bar lets you choose the model, the shape, the quality, how many and the background.
Describe the picture and send it. The x on the Picture bar, Stop making a picture, goes back to talking.
Or just ask for a picture in words, typed or spoken.
To change part of one, open the picture full size and press Change an area. Paint over the part, say what should be there instead, and press Change it. The original is kept.
If no picture service is set up, Make a picture is greyed out and says why.
says: Draw a watercolour of a lighthouse at dusk.
Make the sky in that picture stormy.

lessons.title: Find a chat, start one, rename it
lessons.outcome: After this you know General, a task's chats, and how to find an old chat.
summary: General is the one chat that is always there. Every task has chats of its own, and old chats are found with Search.
how: The Rouh row in the menu always takes you back to General.
To start a chat about a task, open the task's page and press Start chat at the bottom right. The task's chats are listed on its page under Chats.
There is no New chat button in the conversation: a new chat comes from a task, a fork, incognito, or asking Rouh to make a task.
To find an old chat, open Search: the magnifying glass at the foot of the menu, or Ctrl+K. Before you type, it shows Latest chats.
The three dots at the top of a chat rename it, move it to a project or task, make it a task, pin it or delete it. General can never be deleted.
says: Call this chat Holiday plans.
What did I ask you yesterday?
Make this chat a task.

lessons.title: Choose the model for one chat
lessons.outcome: After this you can choose which model answers in a chat.

cover.alt: The model button under the message box, open: Which model answers in this chat, with Cheap, Smart and Auto.

summary: The button under the message box that says Auto, Smart or Cheap chooses which model answers in this chat. A new chat starts on Auto, and once you pick, your new chats start on your pick.
how: Press it. Which model answers in this chat lists the three, each with the model it uses.
Auto lets Rouh pick for each message: Cheap for clearly easy ones, Smart otherwise. You do not have to choose anything.
Cheap always uses the cheaper model: it costs less, and it is less capable. Smart always uses the smarter model: it is more capable, and it costs more.
Your pick holds for this chat, on every device, and your new chats start on it. Pick Auto to go back.
The line at the top of each answer says its time and cost. Press it to see which model answered; Cheaper or Smart there has that answer again on the other.

lessons.title: Read the line above an answer
lessons.outcome: After this you know what the small grey line above each of Rouh's answers says, and what opening it shows.
summary: Above each answer of Rouh's is one small grey line: how long the answer took and what it cost, such as 5.0 s · $0.144. You never need it to use Rouh. It is there for when you are curious how an answer was made.
how: The time is how long Rouh took, from your message to the end of its answer. The cost is what the AI charged for it, in dollars, on the AI account Rouh is set up with.
Press the line to open it. Its title line then also says which model answered and how it was chosen, such as Opus 5.5 · chat set to Auto, and what Rouh looked up in its memory.
Cheaper and Smart on the opened line say which of the two answered. Press the other one to have the same answer again on it.
Under the title line, each step of the answer is a bar on one clock: reading your message, looking things up, the model writing, each tool it used. Press a bar for its details.
Details opens everything kept about the answer, on one page. Press the line again to close it.

lessons.title: Where your request goes
lessons.outcome: After this you know when Rouh answers in the chat, hands work on, or uses the live browser.
summary: Rouh decides how to do what you ask. You never have to choose, but it helps to know what you will see.
how: Most requests are answered in the chat, with Rouh's own tools for mail, calendar, Drive, tasks and the rest, and the model's own web search. Each tool it uses shows as a small line in the answer.
If a step needs your yes, the answer asks with Allow and Not now. Bigger questions go to Decisions.
Bigger work is handed to background work: the answer says so, a branch grows on the orb, and the run is listed in Metabolism. It carries on after you leave the chat.
For a website errand, Rouh opens the Live browser on the canvas. Press Take control to use it yourself, and Hand back when you are done.
says: Find a free hour with Lena next week.
Plan the offsite, and book nothing yet.

lessons.title: Choose what a chat knows
lessons.outcome: After this you can set how much of Rouh a chat uses, and you know how long a chat can get.

cover.alt: Chat Options open above the message box: Full Rouh Capabilities, Simple chat and Custom.

summary: Each chat uses as much of Rouh as you let it. The Chat Options button under the message box, which says Full, Simple or Custom, sets that for this chat.

General keeps its newest 40 messages, with a running summary of what came before. Every other chat is read whole each time; if one grows longer than its model can read, Rouh says so and asks you to carry on in a new chat.
how: Press Full. Chat Options opens.
Full Rouh Capabilities uses everything: what Rouh remembers, your rules, Rouh Tools and LLM Tools. Simple chat is plain talk with the model, with web search.
Custom has four switches: Memory, Your rules, Rouh Tools and LLM Tools. See everything this chat is told lists every rule and piece of context, each with a switch.
Permission, privacy and safety stay on whatever you choose. Reset to defaults goes back to Full.
In a task's chat or a fork, the line under the title, Included content, says what else the chat reads, such as the task's pages. Press it to choose.

lessons.title: Talk in incognito
lessons.outcome: After this you can talk to Rouh without anything being kept.

cover.alt: An incognito chat, edged in orange, with Chat Options open on Simple chat and the Incognito switch on.

summary: An incognito chat is a new chat where nothing is kept. It is deleted when you leave it.
how: Press Incognito, the hat and glasses under the message box. A new chat opens, edged in orange, on Simple chat.
While it is open its messages are kept so it works. Nothing is written to your memory, nothing is searchable, and a reminder set in it is deleted with it.
Leave by pressing Incognito again, or the cross at the top right. If it has messages, Rouh asks first: Keep chatting or Delete and close.
Opening another chat, or closing the tab, deletes it too.

lessons.title: Ask on the side with a fork
lessons.outcome: After this you can ask a side question without changing the main chat.

cover.alt: A fork open beside the chat it came off: 2 / 2 at the top, Forked from Hello Rouh, and its own question and answer.

summary: A fork is a side chat that comes off the conversation where it is now. It has read everything above it, and nothing said in it comes back, so the main chat stays as it was. Use it when something was not clear, or to try an idea on the side.
how: Type the side question, then press Fork, the branch arrow just left of Send. Or press Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter on a Mac.
The fork opens to the right, and the chat it came from narrows to a strip on the left. The arrows and the count at the top, such as 2 / 2, move along the path of forks.

how.text: The chat it came from keeps a mark where the fork came off. Press it to open the fork again.

image.alt: A phone showing the chat: a question, Rouh's answer, the small buttons under each, a fork's mark, and the message box.

how: To fork from an earlier message, press Edit this message and ask again under it, then Fork.
The three dots, then Unlink, turn a fork into a chat of a task you pick.
says: What does that mean for me?

lessons.title: Point at part of a page
lessons.outcome: After this you can show Rouh exactly which part of a page you mean.
summary: When a page from your workspace is open beside the chat, you can show Rouh the part you mean instead of describing it.
how: With a workspace page open on the canvas, press Point.
Click the part of the page to change, then say what should change.
Or select a passage on the page: it goes with your next message.
Above the box it shows as Passage, or the part you chose. Its x lets it go, so you ask about the whole page.
says: Make this shorter.
Turn this into a table.

lessons.title: Keyboard shortcuts
lessons.outcome: After this you know every key the chat answers to.

cover.alt: Keys Rouh answers to: the list that opens when you press the question mark.

summary: At a computer, most things in the chat have a key. Press ? anywhere outside a text box for the list, Keys Rouh answers to. On a Mac, Cmd takes the place of Ctrl.
keys: Fork: send it as a side chat of its own
While Rouh answers, stop the answer; otherwise close what is open, one step at a time
Search chats, tasks, pages, runs and Rouh's own pages
Answer a conflict card with the choice of that number
Move through the navigation's groups, and Search's rows
When nothing has the cursor, starts typing in the message box
On the orb, when it has the focus: send it to that side of the screen
In the picture editor: Brush, Box, Eraser, Undo
how: Press ? to open the list. Escape or Close shuts it.
On a phone each of these is a button instead.

stages.title: Connect your life

lessons.title: Connect Google: Gmail, Calendar and Drive
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can read and answer your mail, keep your calendar and find your files.

cover.alt: The Email and calendar page under Connections, with the Google app's settings and Connect Google.

summary: The one connection that unlocks the most: once it is on, your inbox, your calendar, your Drive and your Docs are all in one conversation.
how: Open the menu (press the orb), then Anatomy, then Connections, then Email and calendar.
The first time on this Rouh, an administrator sets up its Google app on the same page: copy the redirect address into Google Cloud, fill in Client id and Client secret, and press Save.
Press Connect Google, pick your account and allow what Google asks for.
Back in Rouh, the page names the connected account, and this tip ticks itself.
says: What came into my inbox this morning?
What is on my calendar tomorrow?
Find the slides I made last week.
Help me connect my Gmail, one step at a time.

connection.needs: Your Google account. The first time, whoever runs this Rouh gives it a Google app: a client id and secret from Google Cloud.

lessons.title: Hear about new mail as it arrives
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can tell you about mail that matters the moment it lands, or wait until you ask.

cover.alt: The Email and calendar page under Connections, with the Google app's settings and Connect Google.

summary: Gmail tells Rouh the moment a new email lands, so Rouh can sort it and tell you about what matters, instead of waiting for you to ask.
how: Connect Google first: the switch needs Gmail (the tip Connect Google: Gmail, Calendar and Drive).
Flip the switch above to On. Gmail then tells Rouh the moment a new email lands.
Rouh sorts it and tells you about what matters. Flip it Off and Rouh reads your mail only when you ask.
says: Tell me when something important lands in my inbox.
What came in since this morning?

lessons.title: Reach Rouh from your phone
lessons.outcome: After this you can open Rouh in your phone's browser, wherever you are.

cover.alt: The Your Rouh page in Anatomy, with Rouh's address and the button to connect to rouh.land.

summary: Your Rouh at an address of its own, so your phone reaches it as easily as your desk does.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Your Rouh.
Your Rouh's URL is on from birth. If it says Off, press Turn on URL.
Press Show sign-in code and scan it with your phone's camera: it signs you in once, for ten minutes. Then use Share, Add to Home Screen, to keep it like an app.
On the phone, the chat and the canvas take turns, and the orb in the bottom-left corner opens the menu, as on a desk.
says: How can I reach you from the browser on my phone?

connection.needs: A Rouh connected to rouh.land. If this Rouh has no relay, the page says so and there is no address to turn on.

lessons.title: Talk to Rouh on Telegram
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh can message you, and you can answer it, from Telegram.

cover.alt: The Telegram page under Connections, with the steps to make a bot and the box for its token.

summary: Reminders, questions and decisions reach your phone, and you can answer them with a tap.
how: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and answer its two questions. Copy the token it gives you.
Open your new bot and press Start.
In Rouh, open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Telegram.
Paste the token into Bot token and press Save.
says: Send me a Telegram message saying hello.
Remind me on Telegram at five to leave.

connection.needs: Telegram on your phone, and a bot token from @BotFather.

lessons.title: Bring in your iCloud contacts
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh knows the people you know: their numbers, addresses and companies.

cover.alt: The Apple Contacts page under Connections, with the steps for an app-specific password and the Connect button.

summary: Rouh can find anyone in your contacts, show their card and keep it up to date.
how: At account.apple.com, open Sign-In and Security, then App-Specific Passwords. Press +, name it Rouh and press Create. Copy the password.
In Rouh, open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Apple Contacts.
Fill in Apple ID and App-specific password.
Press Connect. Rouh reads your contacts and keeps them in step.
says: Who do I know in Berlin?
What is Lena's phone number?

connection.needs: An Apple ID with two-factor sign-in on, and an app-specific password.

stages.topics: Google mail and calendar, new mail alerts, your phone, Telegram, iCloud contacts

stages.title: Everyday wins

lessons.title: Set a reminder
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh reminds you of anything, at the time you say.

cover.alt: Clockwork: everything Rouh will say or do at a time, by day and hour.

summary: Say what and when, in plain words, and Rouh says it to you at that time: in the chat, and on Telegram if you have it.
how: Say the reminder: what, and a day or a time.
Rouh puts it in Clockwork and says when it will remind you.
Open Clockwork (menu, Work, Clockwork) to see everything coming up, and change or remove any of it.
says: Remind me tomorrow at nine to call the dentist.
Remind me in twenty minutes to take the bread out.
What is coming up?
Move the dentist reminder to ten.

lessons.title: Have Rouh do something on repeat
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh does a piece of work for you every day or week, by itself.

cover.alt: Clockwork, listing work that repeats every day at its time.

summary: Not only reminders: Rouh can do the work itself on a schedule, such as reading your calendar every Monday and telling you the week.
how: Say what to do and how often: every day, every Monday, the first of the month.
Rouh keeps it in Clockwork, marked with how often it runs.
Pause or change it in Clockwork, or by asking.
says: Every Monday at eight, tell me what is on my calendar this week.
Every evening at six, tell me what is still open today.
Stop the Monday calendar summary.

lessons.title: Go through your inbox
lessons.outcome: After this you know what came in and what needs an answer, without opening your mail.

cover.alt: Approvals: the emails and messages waiting for your OK, with the latest case listed.

summary: Let Rouh read the pile and tell you what matters. This needs Google connected (topic 4).
how: Ask what came in and what needs an answer. Rouh sums it up and says who is waiting.
Ask about any one email in more detail, or to find an old one.
When Gmail tells Rouh about new mail as it arrives (the tip Hear about new mail as it arrives has its switch), Rouh tells you about what matters without being asked.
says: What came into my inbox today that needs an answer?
Find the email with last month's invoice.
Who have I not answered this week?

lessons.title: Answer an email with Rouh
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh writes your replies, and you only read and agree.

cover.alt: Approvals, where an email Rouh stopped on waits for your OK.

summary: Say who to answer and what to say, in a sentence. Rouh writes the draft and shows it to you before anything is sent.
how: Ask for a reply: who to, and what to say.
Read the draft Rouh shows you. Change anything, in words.
Tell it to send. Emails Rouh stopped on for your OK wait in Approvals, under Now in the menu.
says: Draft a reply to Lena saying Thursday works for me.
Make it warmer.
Send it.

lessons.title: Plan your day with the calendar
lessons.outcome: After this you can check and change your calendar by asking.

cover.alt: The Morning brief page, where today's calendar is shown.

summary: Your calendar, by asking: what is on, when you are free, and putting things in.
how: Ask what is on a day, or when you are free.
Ask Rouh to put something on your calendar, with a day and a time.
Ask to move or cancel something by naming it.
says: What is on my calendar tomorrow?
When am I free for an hour on Thursday?
Put lunch with Sam on Thursday at one.
Move lunch with Sam to Friday.

lessons.title: Read your morning brief
lessons.outcome: After this your day starts on one page: weather, calendar, news and mail.

cover.alt: Morning brief settings, with its switch, the time it is made and its sections.

summary: Each morning the brief puts the day on one page: the weather, your calendar, a few world stories, unread mail and reminders.
how: Open it from the menu: Now, then Morning brief.
Choose when it is made and what is in it in Morning brief settings (menu, Anatomy, Behaviour).
Its switch is in the next tip, Switch the morning brief on or off.
says: Open my morning brief.
Leave the world news out of my brief.

lessons.title: Switch the morning brief on or off
lessons.outcome: After this you choose whether Rouh makes your morning brief each day.

cover.alt: Morning brief settings, with its switch, the time it is made and its sections.

summary: One page every morning: the weather, your calendar, a few world stories, AI news from your YouTube channels, unread mail and reminders.
how: Flip the switch above. On, a brief is made every morning; Off, none is made.
Off, you can still ask for a brief whenever you want one.
Choose when it is made and what is in it in Morning brief settings.
says: Make me a brief now.
Turn the morning brief off.

lessons.title: Find someone in your contacts
lessons.outcome: After this a person's card, with Call, Text and Directions, is one question away.

cover.alt: A drawing: a question about Lena in the chat, and her contact card on the canvas with Call, Text and Directions.

summary: Ask about anyone by name, or by where they are or what they do. This needs your iCloud contacts (topic 4).
how: Ask about a person.
Rouh answers in the chat and opens their card on the canvas, with Call, Text and Directions.
When someone new writes to you, Rouh offers to save them to your contacts.
says: What is Lena's office address?
Who do I know in Berlin?
Save Sam Rivera's new number.

lessons.title: Connect and control your lights
lessons.outcome: After this you can set the lights in any room by saying so.

cover.alt: The Philips Hue page under Connections, with the Hue app's settings and Connect.

summary: Every Philips Hue light in the house, room by room, on the Home page and by voice.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Philips Hue.
Press Connect and sign in to Hue.
If Rouh cannot reach the bridge, press the round button on top of the bridge, then press Try again within 30 seconds.
Open Home to see every room's lights, or just say what you want.
says: What lights do I have?
Dim the living room lights to thirty percent.
Turn off all the lights.

connection.needs: A Hue account and a Hue bridge. The first time, an administrator gives Rouh a Hue app from developers.meethue.com.

lessons.title: Connect and run your robot vacuum
lessons.outcome: After this you can start, pause and dock the vacuum by saying so.

cover.alt: The Dreame page under Connections, with the account form and Connect.

summary: Clean a room, send the robot home or check its battery, from the Home page or by voice.
how: Open the menu, then Anatomy, then Connections, then Dreame.
Pick the app the robot is in, then fill in your email and password.
Press Connect. If Xiaomi asks for a code, type it and press Verify.
Open Home to see the robot, or just say what it should do.
says: Is the vacuum charged?
Clean the kitchen.
Send the robot back to its dock.

connection.needs: A Dreame robot, and a Dreamehome account with a password (an account made with Apple or Google sign-in has none), or a Xiaomi Mi Home account.

lessons.title: Look something up
lessons.outcome: After this you get a quick, sourced answer without leaving the chat.

cover.alt: A drawing: a question in the chat, and Rouh's short answer with two sources under it.

summary: For a quick fact, ask Rouh to look into it. It reads the web and answers in a few sentences, with the sources it used.
how: Say look into, and the question.
The answer appears in the chat, with its sources numbered under it.
For a proper comparison with a recommendation, say research instead: that comes back as a task (topic 6).
says: Look into what the weather will be like in Lisbon next weekend.
Look into the opening hours of the Lisbon Oceanarium.

lessons.title: Have Rouh use a website while you watch
lessons.outcome: After this Rouh does errands on websites, and you step in when it needs you.

cover.alt: The Live browser page, where Rouh's browser is shown while it works.

summary: For errands on websites, Rouh uses a real browser that you can watch and take over.
how: Say what to do and on which site.
Watch it work in the Live browser (menu, Now, Live browser).
When it needs you, for a login, a code or a payment, press Take control, do that part, then press Hand back.
Rouh never types your passwords and never presses the final Book or Pay for you.
says: Find a table for two on Friday evening on a restaurant's own website, and stop before booking.

stages.topics: Reminders, email, calendar, morning brief, contacts, lights, looking things up

stages.title: Work with tasks

lessons.title: Make a task
lessons.outcome: After this your work has a home, a number and a conversation of its own.

cover.alt: The task browser: every project and task, filed under Work, each with its number.

summary: A task is a home for one piece of work: its steps, its pages and its own conversation.
how: Ask Rouh to make a task, and to break it into steps if you like.
It appears in the task browser (menu, Work, Task browser), filed under Work or Personal, with a number.
Open it to see its steps, and talk about it in its own conversation.
says: Make a task for organising a team offsite in March, and break it into steps.
Open the offsite task.
lessons.without_chat: Without the chat you cannot make a task yet, but you can already see every task and its number: open the Task browser (menu, Work, Task browser).

lessons.title: Add a step and use its number
lessons.outcome: After this you can point Rouh at any piece of work by its number.

cover.alt: A task's page: its title, its number and its first step.

how: Ask Rouh to add a step to a task.

stages.topics: Rouh's memory up close, your team's tools: meetings and Slack, payments, domains, changing Rouh itself; all optional

features.name: The heartbeat
features.what: Rouh's own turn, every half hour in working hours: it checks its duties, carries your quests forward and starts work nobody had to ask for. It only does safe things by itself; anything else comes to you as a decision.
features.off: Off, nothing beats by itself and quests wait; a yes you give in Decisions still runs.

features.name: The morning brief
features.what: One page every morning: the weather, your calendar, a few world stories, AI news from your YouTube channels, unread mail and reminders.
features.off: Off, no brief is made in the morning; you can still ask for one.

features.name: New mail as it arrives
features.what: Gmail tells Rouh the moment a new email lands, so Rouh can sort it and tell you about what matters, instead of waiting for you to ask.
features.off: Off, Rouh reads your mail only when you ask about it.
